Published continuous torque from rest through published rated rpm is assumed; no extrapolation above rated speed. No measured stall thermal map.

Published rotor inertia remains null if unavailable. Simulation uses the explicit upper bound I <= M_motor * R_envelope^2, treating all motor mass at the envelope radius. This is a conservative bound, not a manufacturer rotor-inertia specification.
Complete assembled motor net mass. Drivers, encoders, wiring and custom shaft adapters are not assigned invented masses.

Published body length; conservative circular radius encloses round body or square flange diagonal. Front/rear shaft dimensions are retained in source facts; exact reducer-specific shaft insertion/coupling requires mechanical design.
Exact manufacturer model-specific drawings. CS-11-2XH-A uses nominal diameter 58 mm bounding flange circle and 32 mm axial envelope; generic 82.5 mm page summary is retained as a discrepancy.
Published rated output torque at 2000 input rpm; evaluation restricted to <=2000 input rpm. Repeated/momentary peaks are stored, not used to increase continuous capacity.
Unknown; output limits enforced, separate input-shaft constraint remains unverified.
Ideal lossless reducer and 1:1 local input belts, as in the existing optimization protocol. Published efficiency, friction and backdrive data unavailable; no 75% efficiency is silently substituted.

Pmax is a mechanical rating-limited objective. Voltage/current are retained; electrical current, copper loss and common-bus selection are not optimized. Mixed nominal voltages require suitable supplies/drives.

Approved base edge-frame/mount topology and geometry-derived structural mass/CoM/inertia. L2 fixed 90 mm, J5-to-J6 spacing 110 mm. Belt side rails derive the needed clearance from the actual motor body length, within a 110 mm half-width envelope, rather than an arbitrary 82 mm cap. Physical contact, frame depth and stock-span checks remain enforced. Link lengths compensate to preserve exactly 550 mm reach. Unlimited joints; global self-collision checks off by user request.
